question.text: Cross-holding restriction for MFs per SEBI:

answer.text: Cap on single-issuer exposure (e.g., 10% debt, 10% equity)

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI's Mutual Fund Regulations impose diversification limits to prevent excessive concentration in any single issuer. A widely cited convention is an approximate 10% single-issuer cap for both debt and equity exposure (with separate, calibrated limits for different scheme categories and instrument types), supplemented by sector and group caps. The Trap: "No restriction" contradicts SEBI's prudential framework; 50% and 25% single-issuer exposures are far above the typical caps and would defeat the diversification objective of a pooled vehicle. Note: The Portfolio Managers (NISM-Series-XXI-B) workbook states that mutual fund regulations specify investment limits and that factsheets disclose sector and security exposure, and that PMS agreements can set exposure limits, but does not enumerate a specific 10% single-issuer debt/equity cap on the pages checked. The single-issuer cap framing reflects general industry/regulatory MF practice; exact thresholds vary by scheme category and should be confirmed in SEBI's MF Regulations.
